frequency_question: How often do states successfully sign a water treaty renewal before expiration when faced with bureaucratic and regional political friction?
membership_rule: Includes any formal bilateral water-sharing treaty between sovereign states expiring or up for renewal that faced significant domestic/sub-national friction; excludes unilateral declarations or multilateral conventions.

cases.name: Indus Waters Treaty Permanent Commission annual meetings and continuous operation (India-Pakistan)
Ganges Water Sharing Treaty initial signing (India-Bangladesh)
Columbia River Treaty regime reviews and negotiations (US-Canada)
Lesotho Highlands Water Project Phase II protocols
mekong river commission procedures and agreements

provenance_note: 6 cases named, 7 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 6 named; believed roughly 7 in total for high-stakes bilateral treaties with major federal friction
known_gaps: Excludes minor unverified local basin accords.
skeleton: Total major transboundary water treaty renewal/negotiation instances involving significant federal-state friction since 1985 divided by successful completions within the designated timeframe.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 7 observed major contested negotiations
validity_reason: Treaty negotiation norms and transboundary legal frameworks evolve slowly over decades.
